To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the four axioms of the discounted utility theory imply the existence of a discount function and, with the fifth axiom, the linearity (risk neutrality) of the intra-period utility function; (b) the four and the fifth axioms are independent, and (c) the converse of the fifth axiom is independent of the other axioms.

(1) the preference relation is not risk neutral if and only if the converse to the fourth axiom is false; and (2) the preference relation can be made to be risk neutral without changing the underlying utility function if and only if it satises the fourth axiom.

the discounted utility model is equivalent to a risk neutral model if and only if the converse is satised, and that, if it is not satis ed, then the utility function can be replaced by a linear one without loss of information.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following question: When is a utility function risk neutral?
a generalization of the discounted utility framework that includes risk neutrality and a utility function that may not be risk neutral.
the question of when preferences are risk neutral.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in the absence of topological assumptions, the four axioms and their converse are necessary and suficient conditions for the existence of a linear utility function.

the preference relation induced by a utility function that satisfies the four axioms is not risk neutral if and only if there is no linear utility function that is consistent with the preference relation.
the discounted utility model is risk neutral if and only if the four axioms hold.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
risk neutrality is a necessary condition for the existence of discounting and that, when it holds, it is a consequence of the preference relation.
the converse is a risk-neutralizing axiom, but that the converse is not necessary to ensure risk neutrality.
the converse of the axiom of decomposition is a sufficient condition for risk neutrality, but not a necessary one.
The main takeaway from our work is that
risk neutrality is a consequence of the axiom set and not a primitive assumption.
, in a setting where preferences are not risk neutral, it is possible to construct a utility function that does not depend on a stochastic discount factor.
the converse of the decomposition axiom is the key to the distinction between discounting and risk neutrality.
